audience_problem: Seniors fear missing money/benefits they are entitled to; fear of losing assets to creditors/Medicaid/IRS
topic: Concrete entitlements: "free / owed / cannot be taken" (specific brand or account named)
suggested_angle: Name ONE recognisable retailer/institution and one concrete $0/owed benefit the viewer must ask for
suggested_title: If You're Over 60, [Recognisable Brand] Owes You These N Free Things
thumbnail_concept: Brand logo + big "$0/FREE" + presenter pointing (mirrors Robin MBA template; template itself NOT shown to drive results - subject did)
hook_concept: Open with the specific thing the viewer is currently paying for and not using; state count of items; no preamble
supporting_examples: A4hPtQsiWoA (Costco, PI 445.6); BfOcC1094eo (Aldi, PI 158.9); wafLcwHvn5U (PI 349.9); Kg6NvOExLfc (PI 281.3); counterexamples same template: mRbrwzG4Jow (Airlines, PI 0.17), L1pvT-arh9g (Amazon, PI 2.1)
supporting_principles: DS-000011 Viral Checklist #2 Promise of Transformation, #5 Specificity (supported only weakly in data); Playbook Outlier Concept (topic over packaging)
competition_assessment: DB-only: 11 senior-benefit channels use the pattern; 4/5 channels with enough data positive; large share of breakouts concentrated in few channels; near-duplicate scripts exist across several senior channels
empirical_PI_distribution: free/owed/cannot-touch titles, senior group (n=60): ratio vs rest 2.46 (95% CI 1.20-5.02); 2.48 (1.27-4.86) with cross-channel shared titles excluded (n=58). Descriptive PI quartiles pooled (n=89): 0.47 / 1.10 / 5.57 - wide, heavy-tailed, NOT a forecast
recommended_experiment: Publish 10 matched videos (5 high-recognition subjects, 5 low-recognition subjects) in an identical template to separate "subject recognisability" from template; pre-register success = PI>=2 vs channel baseline at 28 days

audience_problem: Seniors need to know what changes and when, so they can act before it affects them
topic: True deadline / new-rule framing (explicit date, "new rule/law", "starting in")
suggested_angle: Tie one named rule to one dated change and one action
suggested_title: [Agency] Rule Changes [Date]: What To Do Before It Hits Your Account
thumbnail_concept: Calendar/date marker + one number; minimal text
hook_concept: State date, who is affected, and the consequence of inaction in first two sentences
supporting_examples: QhSUdkcVljM (Nia Prescott, "Before October 1", PI 373.5); sNpbDH7IUKw (Madeline, PI 200.4); oPZjqx_6d1g (Housing, PI 566)
supporting_principles: DS-000011 Viral Checklist #6 Urgency or Timeliness
competition_assessment: DB-only: 45 channels used loose date/change language; true-deadline titles n=132 in senior group
empirical_PI_distribution: senior group TRUE-deadline ratio 1.45 (95% CI 1.06-1.97, p=0.020, n=132, shared titles excluded); pooled niche 1.30 (1.01-1.67, p=0.039, n=166). Not significant in investing group (0.95). Exploratory, uncorrected beyond the pattern family
recommended_experiment: Alternate dated vs undated versions of the same topic across 8 weeks; check effect disappears after date passes (decay test)

audience_problem: Seniors fear accounts being frozen / banks acting without notice
topic: Bank-account rules, freezes, thresholds, joint accounts after death
suggested_angle: One specific bank rule + one specific dollar threshold or timing + one protective step
suggested_title: Never Keep More Than $X In One Account After 65 - The Rule Banks Do Not Announce
hook_concept: Describe the bank action the viewer never gets called about
supporting_examples: oPZjqx_6d1g, 0na9DiXBEK8, 3javKka8rUE, Iagjpu1NgcM, HsXxk_4LHmA, SQNY38k8QNU (topic cluster 1, 22 channels)
supporting_principles: DS-000011 Viral Checklist #1 Audience Pain Point
competition_assessment: DB-only: cluster 1 has 22 channels, top channel holds 24% of videos; success rate 37.9% but underperformance 29.5% (high variance)
empirical_PI_distribution: cluster 1 (n=95): median PI 1.18 (95% CI 0.73-1.84 via channel bootstrap), success 37.9%, breakout 28.4%, underperform 29.5%. Cluster-level difference is NOT individually significant
recommended_experiment: Cluster-controlled test: 6 videos in this topic vs 6 adjacent senior topics, same template, same channel

audience_problem: Household decisions with big money stakes (rent vs buy; what changes after paying off a house/debt)
topic: "Real math" comparisons and "what changes after..." life-stage money pivots
suggested_title: Renting Vs Buying a Home - The Real Math
thumbnail_concept: Two-column comparison with one number each
hook_concept: Challenge the common belief with one calculation before the first minute
supporting_examples: nkT_K8l1rEw (Logical Money, 1.73M, PI 258.7); pnJCpIhshX4 (Mark Invests, PI 244.4); sj7tGa1-WWM (Mark Invests, PI 145); 2DBQnxaDScs (Nick Invests, PI 59.9). Identical titles across channels, so NOT independent
supporting_principles: Playbook title family 05 (explainer/comparison) - tested family shows no reliable lift (ratio 1.10, CI 0.93-1.30)
competition_assessment: DB-only: topic appears in 8 videos across 7 channels with outcomes ranging PI 0.3-258 -> demand present but execution/channel-dependent
empirical_PI_distribution: insufficient for a defensible range (n=2-4 per title, shared titles)
recommended_experiment: Check provenance of shared titles (possible cloning); test on an owned channel with two differing thumbnails

audience_problem: Viewers seeking clear explanation of company/economic mechanics
suggested_angle: One mechanism, one company, plain language
hook_concept: Concrete surprising fact within first sentence
supporting_examples: 2T8JrUE_bz4 (Business Decoded, PI 297, 1.46M views); CCXYfrAfW6g, Z1uq829DXlg (large-channel explainers, PI<1 yet 390k/142k views)
competition_assessment: DB-only: group has highest absolute views (median of channel-median views ~152k vs 1.8k-7.2k other groups; Kruskal p=0.0004) but this is confounded with established, larger channels; supply share of explainer-tagged titles only 6.7%
empirical_PI_distribution: Not defensible: absolute views conflate channel scale; group Breakout rate is lowest (6.1%) because baselines are already high
recommended_experiment: Only after external check of search demand; test with 5 videos to measure absolute views vs channel baseline
